environment.description: Deployed on AWS EKS 1.28 with Bottlerocket OS nodes. Pod runs with a securityContext specifying runAsNonRoot:true, readOnlyRootFilesystem:true, and an emptyDir volume (medium: Memory, sizeLimit: 64Mi) mounted at /tmp/hsm-bridge with a projected service account token for IRSA. The node-level containerd configuration sets enable_unprivileged_ports=false and the Bottlerocket host-containers are disabled. AWS CloudHSM Classic cluster (not Luna) is accessed via the cloudhsm-pkcs11 provider with key policy requiring quorum authentication (m-of-n with m=2, n=3) for any CKA_EXTRACTABLE=false key operation. The EKS pod identity association restricts the IAM role to cloudhsm:DescribeClusters only - actual crypto operations go through the PKCS#11 socket which is mounted as a Unix domain socket from a DaemonSet running the CloudHSM client, and that DaemonSet has a seccomp profile (RuntimeDefault) plus a custom AppArmor profile denying all file writes outside /var/run/cloudhsm/. The emptyDir with medium:Memory means the temp files exist only in RAM (tmpfs), never hit disk, and are isolated per-pod (not shared with any other workload). Combined with readOnlyRootFilesystem, no hostPath access, and the memory-backed tmpfs being private to the single pod's mount namespace, there is no path for another process to race or symlink-attack the temp files.
